notes: Fintech sector taxonomy for GFF 2026 exhibitor classification. 'sector' is the single primary bucket used for filtering. 'subSectors' are additive tags drawn from the vocabulary below; a partner may carry subSectors that belong to other sectors' vocabularies (cross-cutting is expected and allowed).

Payments.definition: Moving money between payers and payees: acquiring, gateways, cards, UPI/wallets, POS, payouts, billing, and the software/rails that banks and PSPs run payments on.

Cross-Border & FX.definition: International money movement: remittances, multi-currency accounts, foreign exchange, trade settlement.

Lending & Credit.definition: Originating, underwriting, servicing or collecting credit — lenders (NBFC/HFC/fintech) and the loan software and decisioning stack they run on.

Credit Bureau & Risk Scoring.definition: Credit bureaus and credit-data/scoring providers whose product is the credit information itself.

Banking & Financial Institutions.definition: Licensed deposit-taking and balance-sheet institutions: commercial banks, payments banks, development finance institutions.

Banking Infrastructure & Core Systems.definition: Software and rails sold to banks/NBFCs: core banking, transaction banking, BaaS/embedded finance APIs, switches, agent-banking networks.

Wealth & Capital Markets.definition: Investing, broking, funds, market infrastructure (exchanges, depositories, RTAs) and wealth/financial planning.

Diversified Financial Services.definition: Groups whose own description spans several financial verticals at once (e.g. investing plus insurance plus lending plus payments) with no single dominant line.

Insurance & Insurtech.definition: Insurance carriers, distributors, and the software platforms that issue, price, or service policies.

RegTech & Compliance.definition: Meeting regulatory obligations: AML/CFT, regulatory reporting and interpretation, tax/GST compliance, GRC, consent & data protection, legaltech.

Fraud Prevention & Risk.definition: Detecting and stopping financial crime and abuse: transaction monitoring, merchant risk, scam/ad fraud, risk decisioning.

Identity & KYC.definition: Proving who someone is: eKYC/video KYC, KYB, document and biometric verification, onboarding orchestration, digital identity.

Cybersecurity.definition: Protecting systems and data: cloud/app security, PKI and encryption, offensive testing, AI security.

Crypto & Digital Assets.definition: Blockchain networks, tokenisation, digital-asset custody/exchange, CBDC.

AI & Automation.definition: AI/ML platforms and agents sold as the core product: voice AI, agentic AI, RPA/document AI, process intelligence.

Data & Analytics.definition: Turning data into decisions: BI and data engineering, customer data platforms, account aggregation/open finance, alternative and risk data, observability.

Enterprise Software & IT Services.definition: Horizontal technology not specific to financial services: IT/consulting services, product engineering, databases and cloud infrastructure, devtools, design.

Customer Engagement, CRM & CPaaS.definition: Reaching and serving customers: CPaaS/messaging, WhatsApp business, contact centre, CRM, marketing automation.

Spend & Business Finance.definition: Corporate money management: expense and spend management, corporate cards, payroll, treasury, travel expense.

Loyalty & Rewards.definition: Loyalty programmes, rewards, cashback, gifting and redemption marketplaces.

Hardware & Devices.definition: Physical devices and secure elements: POS terminals, smart cards, biometric capture devices, RFID, secure ID hardware.

Regulator & Public Sector.definition: Regulators, statutory authorities, government bodies and government-promoted financial infrastructure.

Industry Body & Association.definition: Trade associations, self-regulatory organisations and industry councils.

Ecosystem, Investors & Advisory.definition: Accelerators, incubators, VCs and venture builders, trade/investment promotion agencies, country delegations, consultancies and professional advisory firms, industry media and community.

Other Non-Fintech.definition: Real businesses whose stated activity sits outside financial services and financial technology entirely.

Unknown.definition: We hold no evidence — no whatTheyDo text, no useCases, and no informative partner tier — that states what this organisation does. Deliberately not guessed from the company name or from outside knowledge.
